content: The medication omadacycline is approved for the treatment of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) and acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSIs) caused by susceptible microorganisms. The recommended duration of treatment is 7 to 14 days. It has also been granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), including pulmonary disease caused by Mycobacterium abscessus complex (MABc). However, its safety and efficacy in patients under 18 years of age have not been established. In clinical trials for CABP, a mortality imbalance was observed, with 8 deaths (2%) in patients treated with omadacycline compared to 4 deaths (1%) in those treated with moxifloxacin. The cause of this imbalance remains unclear. All deaths occurred in patients over 65 years of age, most of whom had multiple comorbidities. Omadacycline has several drug interactions and contraindications: 1. Oral Retinoids and Tetracyclines: Concomitant use may increase the risk of pseudotumor cerebri (intracranial hypertension). This combination is contraindicated. 2. Amoxicillin, Ampicillin, and Other Penicillins: Omadacycline may reduce the therapeutic effects of these drugs due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor for reduced efficacy if co-administered. 3. Neuromuscular Blockers (e.g., atracurium, cisatracurium, pancuronium, rocuronium, succinylcholine, vecuronium): Omadacycline may enhance the effects of these agents, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Cholera Vaccine: Omadacycline may interfere with the vaccine's efficacy. Avoid co-administration, and do not administer the vaccine within 14 days of systemic antibiotic use. 5. Multivalent Cation-Containing Products (e.g., calcium, magnesium, iron, aluminum): These products can impair the gastrointestinal absorption of omadacycline, reducing its efficacy. Separate dosing by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking these products. 6. Bile Acid Sequestrants (e.g., cholestyramine, colesevelam, colestipol): These agents may reduce the effects of omadacycline. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 7. Vitamin and Mineral Supplements (e.g., multivitamins, folic acid, niacin, selenium): These may decrease the absorption of omadacycline. Separate dosing and monitor for reduced efficacy. 8. Antacids and Alkalinizing Agents (e.g., sodium bicarbonate, citric acid): These may reduce the absorption of omadacycline. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. For oral administration, it is critical to avoid co-administration of omadacycline with products containing multivalent cations (e.g., calcium, magnesium, iron, aluminum) or bile acid sequestrants. These agents can form insoluble complexes with omadacycline, reducing its absorption and efficacy. Proper timing of administration is essential to minimize these interactions.
